newsitem.title: CHINA: China praises gritty official graft busters.
newsitem.headline: China praises gritty official graft busters.

text.p: China on Friday showered praise on the prosecutors who brought down a corrupt local Communist Party chief despite threats and heavy pressure from high-placed friends of the accused.
A court in Taian city in eastern Shandong province in February sentenced party chief Hu Jianxue to death for accepting more than 610,000 yuan ($73,000) in bribes.

The prosecutors who brought Hu to justice had been subjected to threatening telephone calls, malicious rumours and the danger of armed attacks during their eight-month probe into high-level corruption among Taian's elite, the Xinhua news agency said.

Hu had tried to use his power and a network of influential friends to obstruct the investigation, the agency said in a long article that praised the prosecutors for their determination, honesty and commitment.

It said the graft busters "shed blood, sweat and tears in their resolute and moving struggle against corrupt officials," and travelled 490,000 km (304,000 miles), visiting more than 100 towns and cities and interviewing more than 1,400 people.

Their efforts were rewarded when Hu and Taian police chief Li Huimin were sentenced to death for corruption and three other local officials and the head of a state petrochemical firm were given suspended death sentences or terms of life imprisonment.

Corruption, virtually eradicated after the communist revolution in 1949, has boomed under economic reforms launched in 1979 as many government officials rush to convert their political clout into economic gain.
Beijing has launched periodic crackdowns on graft. It trumpets succesful prosecutions, but many Chinese say the campaigns have little long-term effect.
